# Phase Three — Thirty Improvements After Critique

The Awtsmoos renews the plan as surely as the page; Awtsmoos.com must challenge its own elegance before asking users to trust it.

1. Do not migrate archive/test pages merely to improve counts.
2. Identify actual entry routes before touching a family.
3. Never add Future System imports where a route already owns equivalent local systems.
4. Prefer deleting redundant style responsibility over adding another override.
5. Audit selectors for accidental shared-class collisions before changing markup.
6. Preserve every DOM ID consumed by JavaScript unless callers are migrated in the same verified wave.
7. Prefer `min-inline-size: 0` at layout boundaries over scattered overflow hacks.
8. Use `overflow-wrap: anywhere` only for genuinely untrusted identifiers/text.
9. Do not hide overflow to conceal layout defects.
10. Keep sticky elements inside predictable scroll containers.
11. Treat mobile safe-area insets as route-shell responsibilities.
12. Verify keyboard reachability after adding retractable panels.
13. Ensure native `<details>` summaries have hover, active, focus-visible, and open states.
14. Ensure form controls have invalid/disabled/read-only styles where relevant.
15. Avoid hover-only affordances on touch-first surfaces.
16. Add active-state feedback even for links styled as cards/buttons.
17. Avoid animation on layout-heavy properties when transform/opacity can communicate the same state.
18. Keep reduced-motion output functionally equivalent.
19. Use `content-visibility` only on long independent lists, not interactive regions requiring immediate measurement.
20. Keep z-index token ranges small and documented.
21. Browser-check focus rings against actual backgrounds.
22. Browser-check 320px, 375px, tablet, and desktop widths.
23. Measure document scrollWidth after every shell rewrite.
24. Check console and failed network resources after each route-family wave.
25. Run route-specific tests before broad repository suites.
26. Read back every rewritten file in full.
27. Compare planned vs actual files and record delta.
28. Update README/architecture only after implementation proof.
29. Keep procedural-world UI demos under the same local-style contract.
30. Treat any newly discovered global selector or oversized source file as REMAINING_WORK rather than silently accepting debt.
